title: Mark Andrews Wins Oklahoma's First Mackey Award in 2017
question: Who was the first Oklahoma player to win the Mackey Award as the nation's top tight end?
answer: Mark Andrews won the John Mackey Award in 2017, becoming the first Oklahoma player to be named the nation's top tight end. He caught 62 passes for 958 yards that season.
summary: Mark Andrews became the first Sooner to win the Mackey Award as college football's top tight end in 2017, after a 62-catch, 958-yard season.
body: Oklahoma has produced Heisman winners, linebackers who swept defensive trophies and a pile of All-Americans, but until 2017 the Sooners had never had the nation's top tight end. That changed when Mark Andrews was announced as the winner of the John Mackey Award, which the school's athletics site headlined as Oklahoma's first.

Andrews earned it as a junior in a Baker Mayfield-led offense that rarely lacked weapons. He finished the 2017 season with 62 receptions for 958 yards, a figure that placed him among the most productive pass catchers on the team at any position, and he scored eight touchdowns.

The Mackey win capped a steady climb. Over his Oklahoma career (2014-2017) Andrews totaled 112 catches for 1,765 yards and 22 touchdowns. The 1,765 yards are the most by a tight end in school history, according to a 2018 pre-draft profile published by the Green Bay Packers. About one catch in five went for a score.

At 6-foot-5 and roughly 256 pounds, he gave Mayfield a big target who could work the seams, and the award recognized exactly that: a tight end who was as dangerous as a wide receiver. For a program known for its running backs and quarterbacks, the Mackey was a fresh addition to the trophy case, and it remains a good trivia answer for any Sooner fan.
